Commentary.Commentary: So, the target for the Proteas is 232 and they should back themselves to get to the target. However, this pitch is not the regular Wanderers surface and if the Lankan fast bowlers get early wickets, things might change. Join us in a while for the chase.

The man of the moment, Imran Tahir is giving a quick interview before heading back to the pavilion. Says that he just tries to work hard on his bowling and thanks his franchise for backing him. Adds that he is just grateful for every opportunity he gets to play for South Africa. Mentions that it was a great run out by Miller and after that, there was one more stand for Sri Lanka. Is hopeful that his boys will chase down the target. Feels the pitch is on the slower side but it will quicken up as the game progresses as they noticed against Pakistan recently at this venue. Talking about Sri Lanka also having quality spinners, Tahir replies that he is sure that his batters would have made plans against them. On Ngidi also doing well with the ball, Tahir replies that the pacer gave them a good start and it was a good performance from the bowling unit.

Sri Lanka didn't get off to a good start but Kusal Perera and Oshada Fernando anchored the innings with a 76-run stand for the third wicket. The latter was unfortunate to miss out on a debut half century. Dhananjaya de Silva and Kusal Mendis stitched 94 runs for the 5th wicket but once they fell, it was all one-way traffic. The lower order didn't get themselves in and gave away their wickets cheaply.

At 195/4, the visitors looked to get a total near the 300-run mark but that was not to be. Tahir broke the partnership picking up Dhananjaya and then got Mendis later. The leggie ended with 3 wickets while Ngidi who made early inroads picked up the last wicket to bag 3 for himself on comeback.
What a fightback from the South Africans. They have taken 6/36 towards the end and ensured that they do not chase a big total.

Ngidi also finishes with a 3-fer, just like the catcher but the only difference is that the pacer has gone for aplenty. SOUTH AFRICA NEED 232 TO WIN!

Touch and go that but South Africa will be happy to have broken the 94-run stand.

OUT! No half century on debut for Oshada Fernando. The poor chap is well short of the crease and has to go back to the pavilion. A flighted full ball on middle, a googly, Mendis flicks it off his pads to mid-wicket and Miller inside the ring moves swiftly across to his right to make a diving stop. He immediately releases the ball to the keeper as well. In the meantime, Kusal strides out in search of a run but seeing his partner ball-watching initially, he stops. But after that Oshada starts to sprint to the other end without even looking at his partner. Kusal has no other option but to respond. It's a flat throw to the keeper and de Kock breaks the stumps in no time. Oshada tries his best but has no chance of getting in. They appeal and it's referred upstairs. The replays as mentioned already finds the debutant well short of the mark. Oshada was looking so good in his knock and is really unlucky to suffer this fate. South Africa will be delighted to get a couple of quick wickets after a partnership in between.

Brilliant diving effort from David Miller and he has sent in a flat throw to the keeper! Oshada Fernando is in real trouble here. Is he run out? South Africa are celebrating. The debutant is looking disappointed. It seems that he's short. Let's watch the replays...

Good use of the review and Mendis survives.

Had a good time in the Mzansi Super League recently and has bagged a contract with the Kolkata franchise in the Indian T20 League. Let's see how he goes here...

Shorter one on the hips, tucked away for a single to deep square leg.

FOUR! This time, the ball goes further left of the bowler and beats mid off too. No stopping that. Slightly fuller outside off, Oshada drives through the line and gets immaculate timing on that ball to take it to the ropes.
Good shot but straight to the bowler. A length ball outside off, Oshada comes ahead and drives confidently back down the ground. Ngidi puts his hand to the left and stops it at a good height.
Fuller one on the leg stump line, Perera mistimes his flick but the ball goes towards fine leg off the inner half and a single is taken.

On the middle and leg stump line, Perera looks to work it on the leg side but misses the ball. It goes on to hit the thigh pad and lobs onto the surface. Ngidi causing trouble with his extra pace and bounce.
Fuller outside off, Kusal hits it really hard but fails to find the gap as the ball goes straight to the cover fielder.
Ngidi delivers this one on a length and the middle stump line, Perera pushes the ball back to mid on.
Outside edge but safe! A length ball outside off, Perera looks to defend the ball but gets a thick edge that flies well wide of slip for a single down to third man.

Length ball on the middle stump line, Fernando looks to push the ball straight back down but it goes off the inside half and towards deep backward square leg. The call is for two but it is not available.
On the hips, tucked to mid-wicket. No run though as the ball went straight to the fielder there.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through to the keeper.
Solid defense this time, Oshada covers the line of the ball with better foot movement and keeps it out.

Peach! Length ball outside off and it straightens just enough to beat the outside edge of Fernando's bat. Oshada was looking to defend that ball on the front foot but in the end does well to play inside the line.
Guided down to third man for a single by Fernando as he picks up his first run in ODI cricket.
A short of a length ball outside off, left alone by Oshada as he watches the ball all the way into the keeper's glove.

Debutant Oshada Fernando walks in at number 4. He showed good temperament and composure during the Test series and often walked in tough times. Oshada is no alien to this situation and would like to make a strong start in his debut game.

OUT! Tharanga has chopped on! His comeback is not a great one but Ngidi is having a ball in his return game. Back with a bang! He has picked up his second in two overs. A length ball outside off and lots of width on that one, was there to be hit. Tharanga slashes at that ball but unfortunately for him, the ball takes the inside edge and goes back on to disturb his stumps. Early trouble here for the visitors.
Wide! Sprayed down the leg side and it is too far away for Tharanga to put bat on ball there.
Fuller one outside off, it's pushed by Tharanga to mid off but there is no chance for a single this time as the ball is timed too well.
Fuller one outside off, Kusal pushes it to mid off and sets off for the quick single. Makes it easily in the end.

FOUR! Smashed. Ngidi goes a tad fuller outside off and Perera uses the width to thrash the ball away. The ball flies off the bat and in the gap through covers for a boundary. Already an indication of the length that you are not supposed to bowl here.
Slightly shorter length, Tharanga plays away from the body but keeps the ball along the ground towards cover.
Length outside off, confidently pushed to the cover region.
A short of a length ball outside off, Tharanga sways out of the way of the ball and lets it go.

FOUR! Edgy! Short and outside off, Tharanga looks to cut but gets an outside edge to it. The ball goes towards the slip cordon where Faf du Plessis at the first slip region jumps to attempt for the catch. To his dismay, the ball goes over the skipper at second slip and races away to the boundary towards the third man region. Streaky but that's the way Tharanga plays.
The ball holds up a little bit on Tharanga. On a good length on middle, Tharanga looks to push but gets hit on the thigh pad.
Good length delivery outside off, Tharanga shoulders his arms to this one.
Another defensive push from Perera to end the over. A successful one for the hosts.
Back to over the wicket, pushed to the cover region confidently by the new batsman.
Kusal Perera walks out at number 3.

OUT! That is the first one! Ngidi has picked up a wicket in his very first over on his return. He changes the angle and comes around the wicket and bowls this on a short of a good length, Dickwella is early into the shot as he tries to push the ball back down the ground. There is extra bounce and it goes off the top half of the blade and back to the bowler who gobbles an easy catch. Dickwella's stay was a very short one. Not a memorable 50th ODI for him.

Was that a chance? A half-chance you could say! A length ball outside off and Tharanga cuts this one in the air. It seems to have gone towards point on the full but the fielder there does not go for a catch and instead prefers to stop the ball with his left hand. Saves 3 runs for his team though with a half stop.
Left alone outside off this time by the batsman.

FOUR! A four off the first ball for Tharanga as well! This was not that safe though. A length ball outside off and Upul throws his bat at that one and it goes slightly uppishly but in the gap between cover and point. Once it crosses the infield, there is no stopping that.
Lungi Ngidi with the other new ball. Two slips for him as well. Upul to face his first ball...
A length ball outside off and it is pushed to point watchfully for another dot ball to end the over.
Shorter one on the off stump line. Dickwella stands tall and pats this one onto the surface.
Left alone outside off once more. 2 dots follow the 2 fours.
Shortens the length this time, Rabada. Dickwella lets the ball go outside his off stump.

FOUR! Two in two! Already indications that the pitch is a belter. A length ball on the off stump and moves away from the lefty with the angle. Niroshan leans into the drive and finds the gap wide of mid off. The ball races away from the fielders chasing and goes into the rope.
FOUR! What a way to start for Sri Lanka. A fuller length ball with some shape into the left-hander after landing on middle. Dickwella flicks it away beautifully for a boundary through mid-wicket.
A false start! Rabada has lost the ball in his run-up.

We are all set to go now. The South Africa fielders are out in the middle and taking their position. Upul Tharanga and Niroshan Dickwella to open for the visitors. Kagiso Rabada with the new ball in his hand. A couple of slips in place. Everything in readiness, let's play!!!
Both teams line up for their respective national anthems. It's bright and sunny afternoon here in Johannesburg. The stands are slowly filling and it will soon be packed.

TOSS - South Africa win the toss and elect to bowl first. Anrich Nortje makes his international debut for the Proteas. It looks like a pretty balanced XI, although a bit light in experience. For Sri Lanka, Oshada Fernando is making his ODI debut. Their XI is also quite balanced and they have more experienced players compared to the home team.

Hello everyone! Super Sunday in store for all of us. The Wanderers stadium in Johannesburg is beaming down in magnificence. South Africa and Sri Lanka looking primed and ready to get into their coloured-kits showdown. Lasith Malinga will be looking to start off this 5-match series with a win but the first thing he would like to win would be the coin flip. The toss is coming up soon... Stay tuned!
